problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨-2y,\,\frac{x}{2},\,z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2y-x-5$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $-1\le y\le 0.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

*Hint: You're given that the fundamental vector product of $S$ with respect to its canonical parametrization is $||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||=\sqrt{6}.$*
worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that our surface $z=2y-x-5$ can be written using the dot product as 

$$
⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{\overset{~}{n}}=-5,\,\text{or}\,⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨-1,\,2,\,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{-\overset{~}{n}}=5.
$$

Since we require an upward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is positive. This gives us the normal vector

$$
\overset{~}{n}=⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩.
$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $z=2y-x-5$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨-2y,\,\frac{x}{2},\,z⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-2y,\,\frac{x}{2},\,2y-x-5⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(-2y-x+2y-x-5) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(-2x-5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(-2x-5)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+5)\cdot ||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+5)\cdot \sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{1}{\cancel{\sqrt{6}}}(2x+5)\cdot \cancel{\sqrt{6}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-(2x+5)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+5)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{0}\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+5)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-[y]_{-1}^{0}\cdot [{x}^{2}+5x]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(0+1)\cdot (1+5-0) \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$
